answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every new identity must earn its standing the slow way: it stakes a small deposit, then completes a chain of small verified jobs, each receipt signed and hash-linked to the last. A fresh account starts with no credit, like raw timber before it is milled, and cannot climb to the summit of trusted reputation by retelling a fable of past work — one forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the stake. Buying a thousand throwaway identities therefore costs a thousand deposits and a thousand jobs, so forgery pays less than honest work.
